entries.title: Copper wire upgrade caused nationwide flight suspension, US transport secretary says
entries.snippet: The US government is trying to find out whether the chaos was caused by "incompetence" or faulty equipment.

entries.title: US has floated Ukraine ceding Donbas for Nato membership, Zelensky says
entries.snippet: The US has not confirmed the Ukrainian president's comments - a US official told the BBC "many ideas continue to be discussed".

entries.title: Italy fines Meta €805m over accessing users' photos
entries.snippet: The social media giant is accused of not informing 20 million users it had access to their photos.

entries.title: 'Can you believe it?': SpaceX catches part of its Starship rocket on return to Earth
entries.snippet: SpaceX has performed the historic catch using mechanical arms nicknamed "chopsticks".

entries.title: Philippines wins first Eurovision Song Contest Asia
entries.snippet: Front-runner Carmelle emerges victorious with her women's empowerment anthem Sobra-Sobra.

entries.title: Sotheby's auction of $180m Van Gogh challenged over claims it was 'sold under duress'
entries.snippet: Sotheby's says it will work with the heirs of a family who had previously owned the artwork to try and reach a solution.

entries.title: Trump, Putin and Xi plan historic joint meeting in China next week, White House says
entries.snippet: Trump will discuss the "reduction of nuclear weapons" during the unprecedented talks, a spokeswoman says.

entries.title: Arrested generals and a threatened VP: President's son fuels Ugandan succession fever
entries.snippet: The 52-year-old general’s provocative posts and military threats have fuelled rumours of a dynastic succession.

entries.title: Nigeria cautions against travel via Ethiopia's main airport due to altitude
entries.snippet: The foreign ministry in Abuja says 6 Nigerians with underlying health problems have died this year while transiting through Addis Ababa.

entries.title: Hungarian authorities uncover $20m during probe of Orbán-era minister
entries.snippet: Prime Minister Péter Magyar promised a sweeping anti-corruption drive after ousting Orbán in April.

entries.title: 'Miracle on Mississippi' - All passengers rescued after New Orleans cruise ship collision
entries.snippet: The collision leaves 32 people in hospital with non-critical injuries, but no-one unaccounted for.

entries.title: Microsoft says services fully restored after day-long global outage
entries.snippet: Efforts to address the underlying problem with Outlook, Teams and Copilot are complete, the tech firm says.

entries.title: 'We'll get home one day' - US travellers impacted by nationwide ground stop
entries.snippet: Passengers throughout the country were impacted over what the Federal Aviation Administration (FAA) describes as “safety and communication issues”.

entries.title: Watch: Cruise ship overturns after collision with tanker in New Orleans
entries.snippet: Around 130 people were rescued from a cruise ship after it was struck by a tanker while docked in New Orleans, Louisiana on Friday.

entries.title: Watch: Divers explore US ship sunk off Florida coast to create new reef
entries.snippet: The ship was intentionally sunk off the coast of Florida in order to create the world's largest artificial ocean reef.

entries.title: Will the Eurovision Song Contest succeed in Asia?
entries.snippet: The world’s biggest and longest-running song contest is coming to Asia, with eleven countries competing in Bangkok, Thailand on Saturday.

entries.title: Military cemetery decorum: The tradition behind Hegseth's Veterans Day reprimand
entries.snippet: BBC's Bernd Debusmann breaks down why Defence Secretary Hegseth's group was reprimanded at Arlington National Cemetery and the history behind its strict rules of conduct.

entries.title: 'We've got to run': Inside ruined Ukraine power plant under constant drone threat
entries.snippet: Dan Johnson visits one of the country's largest power stations, barely left standing after a ballistic missile strike by Russia.

entries.title: Judo champion shakes up French presidential race with surprise candidacy
entries.snippet: Teddy Riner is one of the most popular figures in modern-day France, and one in five voters say they could support him.

entries.title: My mother told me I would die if I sought treatment for Ebola - I am proof you can survive
entries.snippet: Fear and misinformation surrounds the Ebola outbreak in DR Congo - Dr Kamwanga's mother was not immune.

entries.title: Florida city cancels St. Patrick's Day parade, citing new anti-DEI law
entries.snippet: A new Florida law that prohibits taxpayer dollars from going toward diversity initiatives has prompted Delray Beach to cancel its St. Patrick's Day parade after a nearly 60-year run.

entries.title: Maintenance gone awry caused nation-wide ground stop, says Transportation Secretary
entries.snippet: Transportation Secretary Sean Duffy points blame toward contractor in explaining Friday's nation-wide aviation ground stop.

entries.title: US has lost measles elimination status, global health authorities say
entries.snippet: The U.S. has lost its status as a country where measles is eliminated, according to researchers with direct knowledge of the deliberations at the Pan American Health Organization.

entries.title: SpaceX successfully catches Starship and makes history
entries.snippet: The company's spacecraft returned to its Texas launchpad in dramatic fashion — by carefully lowering itself until two metal arms attached to the launch tower could secure it.

entries.title: Bomb found near ethanol plant in central Illinois forces evacuations
entries.snippet: The bomb was discovered Friday afternoon at the BioUrja Renewables plant in Peoria. Officials say the bomb has been "rendered safe," but called it a "credible threat." The FBI is investigating.

entries.title: 'We can't let them down' -- After midterm wins, Democrats turn to charting path ahead
entries.snippet: Democrats from across the country descended on Denver for a two-day conference to chart the course of their party after sweeping victories in the midterm elections.

entries.title: FAA blames Friday's ground stop on 'equipment issue' during telecoms network upgrade
entries.snippet: Transportation Secretary Sean Duffy said initial investigations pointed to an issue with contractor L3Harris updating old tech at a remote location.

entries.title: Fuel crisis and protests pressure Chile's far-right president
entries.snippet: Chile's far-right President José Antonio Kast is facing mounting public anger, as rising fuel prices trigger transport strikes and protests across the country.

entries.title: Alaska voters aren't ditching ranked choice voting, top-four primaries
entries.snippet: This is the second time Alaskans voted down an effort to repeal the state's unique election system, which voters first approved in 2020. A repeal effort in 2024 also failed narrowly.

entries.title: Perspective: A new kind of White House press secretary
entries.snippet: With the White House press secretary job still left unfilled, maybe an AI assistant might be the answer?

entries.title: Why a problem on the ground can affect flights thousands of miles away among other issues
entries.snippet: Michael McCormick, a former airspace manager with the Federal Aviation Administration, said it could take days for airlines — many of which had to divert flights — to resume normal operations after officials lifted the grounding order.

entries.title: SpaceX's Starship returns from orbit and is captured by launch pad arms in a dramatic first
entries.snippet: It was the grand finale that Elon Musk and his team hoped for — the first-ever capture of a Starship flying back from space. But with the first-stage booster exploding shortly after Friday's liftoff from Texas, the company fell short of its desired double catch.

entries.title: With shifting Iran rhetoric following U.S. elections, Trump leaves Middle East in limbo about path ahead
entries.snippet: Trump's tonal shifts have only added to the uncertainty about what comes next in a war in which America's allies were not consulted before it was started but nonetheless struggle to deal with its economic ramifications.

entries.title: The U.S. flu season is off to a very early start. It's hitting the South and West now
entries.snippet: The Centers for Disease Control and Prevention on Friday posted its latest update, reporting that seven states were reporting high flu activity last week, up from two states the week before.

entries.title: Zelenskyy says a new European security framework floated by U.S. could benefit Putin
entries.snippet: European leaders have stressed that decisions about the continent's security must be made by Europeans themselves, warning against allowing Russia to dictate the terms of a new security order or negotiate NATO's future.

entries.title: New Orleans port sues to get control of tanker that crashed into cruise ship on Mississippi River
entries.snippet: The lawsuit, filed by the Board of Commissioners of the Port of New Orleans, said the Atlantic Asphalt tanker caused at least $1 million in damage to its terminal. A judge issued a warrant Friday giving federal officials control of the ship for now.

entries.title: Alaska voters reject ballot measure seeking to repeal open primaries and ranked voting system
entries.snippet: The ballot measure, decided as part of the Nov. 3 election, marked the second time in two years that voters have rejected attempts to overturn the system and revert to partisan primaries and to general elections in which just one candidate can be selected.

entries.title: What to know about flights after the U.S. nationwide ground stop
entries.snippet: The longest flight stoppage in 25 years ended around 8:15 p.m. ET Friday, allowing some domestic flights to take off from U.S. airports. Officials expected a full recovery by Sunday.

entries.title: Democrats try out a strange new emotion at post-midterms What's Next conference: hope
entries.snippet: Democrats spent two days chewing over their future at the What's Next conference and trying to deal with the fact that it looks, for a moment at least, quite bright.

entries.title: U.S. gives states another 6 months before they have to remove people from Medicaid for not working
entries.snippet: The administration clarified that while states still have the option to take action at the beginning of the year, they won't have to kick anyone off or deny coverage for failure to meet the requirement until July 1.

entries.title: WATCH: Rubio delivers keynote address at Federalist Society National Lawyers Convention
entries.snippet: Rubio gave a sweeping speech to fellow conservatives on Friday evening acknowledging that Americans are struggling in the current economy, while also railing against what he called the "weaponization" of international law to constrain the U.S. from acting in its own interests.

entries.title: Jonathan Kreiss-Tomkins becomes first Democrat since 1998 elected governor in Alaska
entries.snippet: His victory means Democrats will control the governor's office in 30 states, including several they flipped after years of Republican control in places such as Iowa, Georgia, Ohio and Texas.

entries.title: Microsoft says services fully restored after global outage
entries.snippet: The outage affected governments, courts, healthcare services, businesses, airlines and banks in many places. Governments including those of Japan, Singapore and Australia reported that the hourslong episode had impacted some of their operations.

entries.title: Thousands of flights canceled as airlines work to recover from nationwide ground stop
entries.snippet: The nationwide stop was the first since January 2023, when a key FAA computer system that sends notices to pilots malfunctioned, and the second since the Sept. 11, 2001, attacks.

entries.title: SpaceX's Starship soars into orbit after booster malfunction thwarts double catch attempt
entries.snippet: SpaceX's attempt to recover its entire Starship back at the launch pad was thwarted when the booster malfunctioned and ended up in the water Friday, but the spacecraft still soared into orbit in its boldest test yet.

entries.title: FAA issues rare nationwide ground stop due to 'extraordinary circumstances'
entries.snippet: Air travel across the country came to a standstill on Friday after the Federal Aviation Administration issued a rare nationwide ground stop citing "extraordinary circumstances" and "reasons of safety." Aviation correspondent Miles O'Brien reports.

entries.title: News Wrap: Tanker crashes into river cruise boat in New Orleans

entries.title: Bessent accuses Lutnick of failing to prevent China from obtaining Nvidia chips
entries.snippet: The fallout of Jensen Huang's downfall expanded into a public fight between two of President Trump's top advisers. Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent accused Commerce Secretary Howard Lutnick of failing to prevent China from obtaining Nvidia's most advanced chips. Nick Schifrin loo

entries.title: Increasing cost of housing squeezes Americans out of market
entries.snippet: Sales of existing homes in the U.S. fell last month to their lowest level in more than 16 years. That's according to a new report by the National Association of Realtors. In October alone, sales dropped to 3.75 million homes, an 8.8% drop compared with the same time last year. St

entries.title: Does Van Hollen have enough support to beat Schumer in Senate leadership race?
entries.snippet: Senate Democrats won back their majority last week, and now they're fighting over who will lead it. Maryland Sen. Chris Van Hollen has thrown his hat in the ring and says he will take on current Democratic leader Chuck Schumer. Congressional correspondent Lisa Desjardins reports

entries.title: DW
entries.snippet: News, Analysis and Service from Germany and Europe - in 30 Languages

entries.title: SpaceX carries out first-ever spaceship capture
entries.snippet: The successful recovery of SpaceX's Starship marks a breakthrough in founder Elon Musk’s goal of developing a fully reusable rocket system.

entries.title: Germany's 2027 budget: A record €561 billion and a mountain of debt
entries.snippet: The 2027 federal budget proposal has finally been hammered out and is set for a vote in parliament. What are the government's policy priorities in defense, infrastructure, the economy and social spending?

entries.title: Nigeria's upcoming election marred by rising AI disinformation
entries.snippet: As Nigeria inches closer to the 2027 polls, the use of artificial intelligence in the electoral process has prompted questions about integrity and institutional readiness. Can Nigerians trust their democratic processes?

entries.title: South Sudan pushes back elections amid violent flare-ups
entries.snippet: South Sudan has been independent from Sudan since 2011, and has not yet held national elections. Since then, the country faces cycles of violence after a civil war led to a tenuous peace deal.

entries.title: US: Duffy says 'incompetence' or bad tech to blame for flight haltings
entries.snippet: Air carriers in the US canceled some 16,000 flights over the past 24 hours in the biggest such grounding since 9/11. Officials hinted that incompetence or faulty equipment, not malfeasance, is the cause.

entries.title: Fact check: 'Iranian' content farms reach millions
entries.snippet: Several social media accounts claiming to represent the Iranian military show signs of being part of so-called content farms. DW Fact Check looks at how they operate and how users can spot them.

entries.title: Italy slaps Meta with €805mn fine over access to Android photos
entries.snippet: Italian regulators say Meta accessed photos and multimedia content from Italian users via the Facebook application for Android devices. Meta said it would appeal the decision, calling the fine "disproportionate."

entries.title: COP31: Protesters, UN urge swift climate deal
entries.snippet: The UN climate chief has warned that "tactical delays" at the COP31 climate talks in Turkey could prevent a deal to slow global warming.

entries.title: Werner Holzer Prize awarded to Katja Gloger and DW's Jaafar Abdul Karim
entries.snippet: DW journalist Jaafar Abdul Karim and Russia correspondent Katja Gloger have been awarded the prestigious Werner Holzer Prize for international journalism.

entries.title: Ukraine: Zelenskyy says security deal could go to referendum
entries.snippet: The US has broached the idea of Kyiv giving up the Donbas region in exchange for NATO membership, the Ukrainian president said.

entries.title: New facilities in Laos and Cambodia: Is China expanding its military presence in Southeast Asia?
entries.snippet: China has been growing its economic relationships in Southeast Asia. Now new military facilities in Laos and Cambodia are causing smaller countries to worry China's military networks are also expanding.

entries.title: Germany news: Solar power production approaches record high
entries.snippet: Solar power output in Germany in 2026 has already surpassed last year's total. Meanwhile, experts say the country is headed for a budget crisis. DW has more.

entries.title: Wolf Biermann at 90: The singer who defied East Germany
entries.snippet: His life is a reflection of contemporary German history, which Biermann has addressed via his songs and sharp wit. Turning 90, he’s as feisty as ever.

entries.title: Hungary: Millions in hidden cash found in Orban graft probe
entries.snippet: Investigators discovered bundles of banknotes buried in forests and concealed in buildings. The money was seized during an investigation into a former minister accused of accepting millions in bribes.

entries.title: US loses measles-elimination status after 26 years, WSJ reports
entries.snippet: The Pan American Health Organization has reportedly stripped the US of its measles-elimination status after 26 years, as the country battles its worst outbreaks in more than three decades.

entries.title: Microsoft says all services working again
entries.snippet: US tech giant Microsoft says it has fixed problems that led to a global outage of its services. The glitch severely disrupted online communications in businesses and governments for more than 24 hours.

entries.title: Sudan: Misery worsens amid plummeting aid for displaced people
entries.snippet: Sudan's humanitarian crisis is exacerbated by cuts in international aid. Almost 34 million people are in need as war and drone strikes are making it difficult to deliver aid to the population.

entries.title: Turkey uses espionage accusations to pressure government critics
entries.snippet: The arrest of a German foundation's employee in Istanbul this week has put the focus back on pressure tactics used by the Erdogan administration. The arrest is far from the first of its kind.

entries.title: India: Delhi surpasses Lahore as world's most polluted city
entries.snippet: Delhi's Air Quality Index (AQI) was recorded to be higher than Lahore in Pakistan on Friday, which made it the most polluted city globally.
